question: Does a different public source offer explicit time-series channels suitable for a bounded temporal qualification?
selection: TD2D descriptor identified manD as a takeover dataset with vehicle-state records. Selected for measurement availability; not a broad ranking or superiority claim. Separate screen frozen before these direct captures.

dataset.title: manD 1.0
dataset.interpretation: Dataset title 1.0 and Dataverse release 2.0 are distinct identifiers. Unrestricted is the retained metadata state, not a promise of future availability.

primary_documentation.scope: Documents time-series file structure and scripted takeover scenarios; neither documentation nor a descriptive event label proves actual outcome timing.

dictionary.name: DataInfoSheet.xlsx
dictionary.inspection: Read-only ZIP/XML stored values and cell coordinates, no edits, recalculation, spreadsheet export or upstream code execution. Source bytes unchanged.
dictionary.time_limit: Time descriptions mention rate 256; the inspected unit cells have no stored value. Origin, numeric unit, interpolation and actual cross-file alignment remain unresolved. A delivered 256 Hz grid must not be treated as native event precision; nominal native spacing is 50 ms, not a proved error bound.

event_codes.meaning: accident-detected message; prompt to continue driving

missing_sentinel.meaning: distance unavailable, not a measured large safe distance

dictionary.event_limit: Environmental scenario code, system message, driver action, automation transition, measured collision and recovery are different observations. Event onset/offset persistence, message latency and relation to ego-vehicle failure are not qualified by these names.

acquisition.source_scope: Official structure page, repository metadata, primary article and released dictionary only. Original payloads remain private.

next_executable_step: Under a new bounded protocol, retain the small AvailableData coverage workbook and read DataExtraction.py as source; do not execute it. Establish which public runs contain the required vehicle/environment channels and how nested archives can be inspected safely.

Freeze metadata-based sample selection, request/storage/decompression/time bounds, eligible streams and event/clock checks before opening trial outcomes. The smallest participant archive is already 59,858,301 bytes; none fits this owner's 2 MiB response cap. Do not select the shortest archive as if it were a complete representative run.

Admit only permitted vehicle/environment records for a bounded observation check. Verify actual time units, origin, monotonicity, cross-channel alignment, native resolution, code onset/offset and recording termination. Keep missing/sentinel values distinct from zero or successful recovery.
Stop without constructing recovery labels if capture timing, collision meaning or monitored follow-up/censoring cannot be qualified. A documentation lead alone cannot admit readiness modeling.
